purpose: Temozolomide is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of brain tumors, including glioblastoma multiforme and astrocytoma. It is often used after surgery and radiation therapy to help slow or stop the growth of cancer cells in the brain.
how_it_works: Temozolomide works by attaching itself to the DNA inside cancer cells, which damages the DNA and prevents the cancer cells from being able to copy themselves and grow. Think of it like putting a roadblock in the cancer cell's instruction manual so it cannot keep multiplying. Healthy cells can sometimes repair this damage, but cancer cells often cannot, which helps target the tumor.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting are very common, especially right after taking the pill — your doctor will likely give you anti-nausea medicine to help. You may also feel very tired, lose your appetite, have headaches, or feel constipated. Your blood cell counts will drop, which can make you more likely to get infections, bruise easily, or feel weak.
warnings: Because this medicine lowers your immune system, you are at higher risk of serious infections, including a rare but dangerous lung infection called PCP pneumonia — your doctor may give you a preventive antibiotic. You must have regular blood tests to monitor your blood counts. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can seriously harm a baby. Men and women should use effective birth control during treatment and for several months after. Avoid contact with people who are sick while on this medication.
typical_dosing: Temozolomide comes as a capsule you swallow whole, usually taken once a day on an empty stomach or with a light meal. For brain tumor treatment, a common approach is taking it every day for 42 days during radiation, followed by rest cycles where you take it for 5 days in a row, then rest for 23 days. Your doctor will calculate your exact dose based on your height and weight, and it is very important to take it exactly as prescribed — never open or crush the capsules.
